speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter disease (likely chronic or recurrent) or early-onset pigmented villonodular synovitis (PVNS) given the severity at night and young age; however, the normal CRP and mild ESR make septic arthritis or typical rheumatoid arthritis unlikely. I will proceed with a detailed physical exam to check for a tibial tubercle prominence or joint effusion characteristics.
